---
name: Never force push or overwrite repos
description: Never suggest git push --force or overwriting existing repos/branches without explicit confirmation
type: feedback
---

Never suggest `git push --force` to overwrite an existing repo, even if it looks like an old PoC.

**Why:** The existing content might have value, context, or history that isn't obvious. Force-pushing destroys that permanently.

**How to apply:** When pushing to a remote that already has content, always suggest creating a new repo/branch or fetching first. Never default to `--force`.
---
name: feedback-merge-just-commit
description: "Don't run full lint/prettier/tsc passes to \"verify\" a merge — resolve conflicts, commit, push. Both sides already passed their own checks."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: c225d886-900b-4a51-bb80-c772a2963347
---

When merging `main` (or another branch) and conflicts come up, resolve the conflicts and commit. Don't run a full `eslint`/`prettier`/`tsc` sweep across the package "to verify the merge" — both sides already passed their own checks, and pre-existing errors on either side aren't the merge's problem.

**Why:** Sid called this out directly during the main → migration-block-init-staging-branch merge. The rule "run all three checks after changes" was over-applied to merge commits, which exposed pre-existing TS errors in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts` that had nothing to do with the conflict resolution.

**How to apply:**
- For merge commits, focus on conflict resolution correctness, not full re-verification.
- If a conflict resolution looks structurally risky (picked the wrong side, signature mismatch, etc.), do a targeted `tsc --noEmit` on the affected files — not the whole repo.
- Never `git stash` mid-merge to "compare with the pre-merge state." That loses merge state and is destructive. If you need a before/after, use `git show MERGE_HEAD:path` or `git show HEAD~:path` instead.
- Related: [[feedback-pr-scope-discipline]] — merge commits stay scoped to the merge, no opportunistic fixes.
---
name: Minimal merge commit messages
description: For merge commits, use the default git message (one line) — don't write a prose summary of conflict resolutions
type: feedback
originSessionId: da05784b-debd-4e50-9818-223758823d5d
---
For merge commits, use a one-line message — `"Merge origin/main into <branch>"` or whatever the default would be. Do NOT write a multi-paragraph summary of which conflicts were resolved or how.

**Why:** The diff already shows what was resolved. A long prose message in the merge commit body adds noise that the reviewer has to wade through. Past merges on this branch use the default one-liner.

**How to apply:** When committing a merge, use `git commit -m "Merge origin/main into <branch-name>"` — short, matches existing merge commits on the branch. Skip the "here's what I resolved" commentary. Conflict-resolution reasoning belongs in chat, not in the commit message.
